mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC fell in every one of the last four weeks (-34.7 to -44.7) and TRANSIT fell in lockstep, so the same containment-driven suppression of trip generation persists and the next four-week mean stays below the last four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined 10.0 points from t-3w to t-0w
fact:TRANSIT declined 10.0 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is greater than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Once the weekly RETAIL_REC decline crosses 4.0 points the drop is accelerating rather than drifting; the acceleration feeds on itself through trip-avoidance learning and persists at least two more weeks, dragging the next 28-day mean below the last.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC posts a week-on-week decline of at least 4.0 points (satisfied at t-1w and t-0w)
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly deltas were -0.9, -4.1, -5.0 points across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: After any week with a RETAIL_REC decline of 4.0 points or more, RETAIL_REC recovers to its pre-decline level within 14 days in more than half of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: The joint collapse of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES removes the office-and-commute anchor for weekday discretionary trips; when both fall together the retail channel loses its captive footfall and neither series alone can offset the loss, so RETAIL_REC declines further over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall at least 3.0 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell 3.9 points and WORKPLACES fell 4.1 points at t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall at least 3.0 points, the following 28-day mean RETAIL_REC is at or above the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Falling GROCERY_PHARM (-20.3 to -30.4) while RESIDENTIAL rises to +6.6 shows households have abandoned forward-buying and consolidated into minimal, destination-specific trips; that trip-thrift spills over into retail-and-recreation within one week and caps the next four-week mean below the last.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls at least 4.0 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL is above +5.0
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell 5.5 points at t-0w while RESIDENTIAL rose to +6.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises week-on-week in the seven days following a GROCERY_PHARM drop of 4.0 points or more paired with RESIDENTIAL above +5.0.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT breaking below -50 (from -48.7 to -52.6) marks a hard restriction regime; whenever the transit series crosses that level, official capacity limits on indoor venues follow within two weeks and clamp retail-and-recreation footfall below its prior level.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses below -50.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT crossed -50 for the first time at t-0w (-52.6)
failure_condition: In the four weeks after any TRANSIT crossing below -50, the mean RETAIL_REC exceeds its level over the preceding 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS fell 17.3 points over three weeks (-4.7 to -22.0), consistent with end-of-summer outdoor activity rolling off; the same seasonal roll-off removes warm-weather leisure excursions that previously lifted retail-and-recreation, so the next four-week mean falls below the last.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined monotonically from -4.7 to -22.0 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: PARKS rebounds above -15 within two weeks while RETAIL_REC remains below its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL is saturating (+5.0, +4.7, +5.3, +6.6) and cannot absorb much more at-home time; once the residential series stops gaining more than one point per week the confinement channel is exhausted, downward pressure on RETAIL_REC dissipates and the next four-week mean exceeds the last.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL week-on-week change drops below +1.0 point
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL weekly gains decelerated to +1.3 then flattened near a +6.6 ceiling
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL gains less than one point week-on-week for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC still falls over the following 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Under an active tightening regime the week-on-week fall in WORKPLACES (-1.0, -5.9, -4.1) is the fastest-moving policy lever; when workplaces shed more than 3.0 points in a week, retail-and-recreation follows within one week and the next four-week mean undercuts the last.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly change is -3.0 points or lower
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 5.9 then 4.1 points at t-1w and t-0w while RETAIL_REC fell 4.1 then 5.0
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES falls 3.0 points or more, the following 28-day mean RETAIL_REC is at or above the preceding 28-day mean.
